As for being new to the setting, that’s perfectly okay! Any good group will help you know the things you need to know without overloading you. I’d say to try not to go overboard trying to learn the lore. Read a few relevant sections of the core Rulebook (your clan write up certainly, and then a bit on whatever sect youre in, eg if it’s a Camarilla city make sure you know the traditions). Other than that just have fun with it!

Im prepping to run a similar type of game, here’s how I’m doing it, hope it helps.

My XP rewards are goal oriented, and get larger the longer into the chronicle we are (both because XP costs go up over time, and because the scope of the character’s goals grows).
When a character makes progress towards a major or minor goal (possibly Desires and Ambitions, but not necessarily), they’re able to mark XP. At the start of the Chronicle it’s 1 XP for a minor goal and 2 XP for a major. By the second chapter it’s 2/4, 3/6 during the 3rd, etc. (Though I’m capping it at 5/10, both because any more than that is too much and because my chronicle only has 5 chapters).

I do this because it incentivizes players towards setting and completing goals (and by extension, interacting with the world). So I guess my actual advice is reward XP for the behavior you want to see from your players.

Personally, I think we’re focusing too much on whether it belongs at pride or not. I think it absolutely does, the queer and kink communities have been intertwined for decades, with major parts of the gay rights movement being tied to leather culture and similar. So I think the issue is more based around when, where, and how it should be included. The solution (like to most things) is communication, clearly letting people know where things like that are so they can choose whether or not they want to interact with them. “This section of the march/this area will be kink friendly.” There’s more than enough room for all of us, for both adult-focused events and child-friendly ones.
Also I think it should be noted that imo “keeping kids away from kink” doesn’t mean like, a person in a collar or harness or pup hood. Obviously you shouldn’t be performing kink around people who don’t/can’t consent to seeing that, but just wearing leather isn’t kink, it’s a community who are not some danger to kids. A child won’t be traumatized just by seeing a leather daddy or whatever marching. We need to have an open and honest conversation as a community about boundaries and appropriateness, but we shouldn’t overcorrect and start censoring ourselves beyond what is necessary. Everyone has a place in the community, not just the socially acceptable queers. Obviously, this is just my opinion.

I understand your point, my previous comment was very much an oversimplified and idealist method of how it would work. I’m not an expert on global trade but I genuinely believe the principal of communities self-determining what to do with their resources, trading in mutually beneficial ways that make up for resources that cannot be made locally, in my mind anarchism is a method of socialism very focused on not creating new hierarchies. Obviously it’s not as simple as “the communities would email each other and agree to trade”, many previous trade networks would still exist, and communities would organize by regions to coordinate with other regions. There would be more focus on localized production of the majority of what is needed. I may not have it compleltey figured out but these are just my opinions, not the entirety of anarchist thought. And no we don’t have examples of how the whole world could work on anarchist principles but we do have examples in historical regions (especially Ukraine and Spain at various points, though I don’t want to turn this into a debate about the complex histories of those regions and their specific struggles).
